body:
`case_study:dhfl-2019` | 2019-06-04 | tickers: DHFL | confidence: verified

Dewan Housing Finance peaked near Rs 690 in Sep 2018. On 21 Sep 2018, right after IL&FS defaulted, DSP MF sold DHFL commercial paper at a steep yield and the stock fell up to ~60% intraday. Jan 2019: Cobrapost alleged ~Rs 31,000 cr routed to shell companies linked to the Wadhawan promoters; the stock fell 23% in three sessions (Rs 209 to Rs 162). Jun 2019 the company missed bond/CP payments; Nov 2019 RBI took over the board and made it the first NBFC under IBC; Piramal acquired it in 2021 (~Rs 34,250 cr plan) and listed equity was effectively wiped. Visible flags: (1) asset-liability mismatch: 15-20-year home and builder loans funded by short CP and MF money; (2) fast AUM growth into wholesale/developer loans, many to little-known entities with promoter links (Wadhawans also controlled HDIL, the borrower that later sank PMC Bank); (3) thin spreads and leverage ~10x+; (4) heavy MF ownership of its CP = run risk; (5) an auditor's 'no indication' rebuttal of Cobrapost in Mar 2019 produced an 11% bounce that turned out to be a bull trap. Lesson: for lenders, the funding structure (tenor of liabilities vs assets) and borrower concentration matter more than reported NPAs; a sharp rise in CP spreads is a market signal before ratings move.

**Lesson:** Check ALM buckets and wholesale-book borrowers; market spreads lead ratings
**Spotted early by:** Cobrapost investigation; debt-market sellers (DSP MF)
**Links:** illustrates -> `insight:disqualifiers`, illustrates -> `insight:lender-blowup-signals`, caused_by -> `case_study:ilfs-2018`
**Sources:** <https://theprint.in/governance/promoters-of-housing-finance-major-dhfl-swindled-rs-31000-crore-alleges-cobrapost/184961> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/amp/article/markets/dhfl-hits-35-month-low-falls-27-in-three-days-119013000276_1.html> ; <https://www.business-standard.com/article/pti-stories/dhfl-shares-spurt-11-pc-after-auditor-report-on-fund-diversion-allegations-119030600962_1.html> ; <https://qz.com/india/1860466>

|---|---|---|---|
| 0–3 | **Auditor's report**: opinion type, Emphasis of Matter, KAMs [CAMs], auditor name and tenure; IFC report [Item 9A ICFR] | Standalone + consolidated audit reports [Item 8, 9A] | Qualified/adverse/disclaimer; IFC material weakness; auditor changed mid-term |
| 3–7 | **CARO 2020** 3(ix), 3(xi), 3(xviii), 3(iii), 3(xix), 3(ii)(b), 3(vii) [8-K items 4.01/4.02, NT 10-K] | Standalone audit report annexure | Default, fraud, auditor resignation with issues, material uncertainty |
| 7–12 | **Cash test**: 5-yr Σ CFO / Σ PAT; Σ FCF (lease-adjusted); CFO before WC vs WC change | Cash-flow statement (5 yrs from Screener/XBRL) | Σ CFO/PAT < 0.5 with no clear capex/WC reason |
| 12–16 | **Working capital**: DSO incl. unbilled, DIO, DPO trend; supplier-finance/factoring note | Balance sheet + notes | DSO/DIO up >15 days/yr for 2+ yrs without explanation |
| 16–19 | **Other income & exceptionals**: OI/PBT; 5-yr Σ exceptionals / Σ PAT; ETR vs 25.17% [21%+state] | P&L + notes | Core PBT < 0 presented as profitable |
| 19–23 | **Balance sheet**: CWIP ageing; capitalised interest/dev; goodwill+intangibles vs equity; lease liabilities; contingent liabilities / net worth; guarantees | Notes + Schedule III additional info | Guarantees to group > 25% of NW; CWIP >3y > 25% of CWIP |
| 23–27 | **Related parties & promoter**: RPT note (sales, purchases, loans, guarantees, ICDs, royalty); AGM RPT resolutions; pledge %; promoter holding trend [DEF 14A Item 13, Form 4] | RPT note; AGM notice; NSE/BSE filings | Loans to promoter entities; rising pledge >25% |
| 27–30 | **Scores & write-up**: Beneish M (non-financials), Altman Z/Z'', Piotroski F (cheap stocks only), Sloan accruals; fill the template; one-line verdict | Your sheet | ≥3 red flags → no position without variant perception |

**Banks, NBFCs and insurers:** skip Beneish, Altman and Sloan. Use asset-quality (GNPA/NNPA trends, SMA-2, restructured book, write-offs vs provisions), ALM gaps, the CRAR trend, related-party lending, RBI divergence disclosures, and auditor KAMs on ECL.

- [ ] **No inbound ports open to the internet.** Nothing on the Pi needs to accept connections from outside.
  Remote Control and git work over outbound connections only. Keep the router's port forwarding off for the Pi.
- [ ] **Separate user account** on the Pi for this work (e.g. `fein`), not `pi`/root. Run cron jobs and Claude as that user.
- [ ] **SSH keys only** (disable password login: `PasswordAuthentication no` in `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`), or turn SSH off if
  you use the Pi only via screen and keyboard.
- [ ] **Firewall:** `sudo apt install ufw && sudo ufw default deny incoming && sudo ufw default allow outgoing && sudo ufw enable`
  (add `sudo ufw allow from <your-LAN-subnet> to any port 22` only if you use SSH on the LAN).
- [ ] **Kite wrapper binds to `127.0.0.1` only** (not `0.0.0.0`), and is read-only (no order/funds/holdings endpoints).
  If you want it reachable from your laptop, use a private network like Tailscale rather than opening ports.
- [ ] **Secrets in files with `chmod 600`** under `~/fein-data/secrets/`, owned by the `fein` user. That covers the Kite API key/secret/access
  token, Screener cookies and the GitHub token. **Never commit them.** I'll add `secrets/` to `.gitignore` patterns.
- [ ] **GitHub access:** a *fine-grained* token limited to `aditya-bad/fein`, with contents read/write only and an expiry date.
- [ ] **Automatic security updates:** `sudo apt install unattended-upgrades && sudo dpkg-reconfigure unattended-upgrades`.

**The L18 rule (≥5 per category, ≥2 peers) is met three times:** WTS revenue and margin, and AOS revenue and other. Everything else is pooled. The peer medians are 100% in most categories, so **any** shortfall produces a negative SAC. That is why Lincoln (88.5%, one partly) gets −11.5. US peer medians are a harder bar than India's.

| cos_7 Q1 (MD&A changed) | +1.0% | −0.1% | −9.5% [−31.5, +3.9] | −15.7% | −10.7% | 38.7% | −2.13 |
| jac_7 Q1 | +1.9% | +5.5% | +3.4% [−8.2, +27.4] | −6.0% | +1.0% | 45.6% | +0.58 |

Other secondary cuts (none changes a verdict):
- **H1 vs size-only controls (v1 method):** −1.1% (t −0.20). Vs IWM: +0.6%. Raw 12 m return of changers: +14.6% mean, −5.2% median.
- **H1 by filing year:** 2024 +1.3% (t +0.2); 2025 −4.2% (t −0.5). **H2:** 2024 −1.4%; 2025 +2.7%.
- **Ex-biotech:** H1 −1.3% (t −0.2), H2 +2.3% (t +0.5).
- **Outliers:** the H1 mean is pulled up by a handful of huge winners. ASTS was about +970% from its 2024
  filing, and BE, UUUU, COGT and AGX each rose about +300–540% from their 2025 filings (spot-checked; the
  moves are real, not split errors). This is why the winsorised mean (−4.0%) and the median (−10.5%) sit well
  below the mean.

**Pattern worth noting (hypothesis only):** in both v1 and v2, changers have a low median excess (v1 −14%, v2
−10.5%) and a low hit rate (38–40%, against ~50% for non-changers), while their mean is rescued by a fat right
tail. Big text changes look less like "drifts down" and more like "lottery ticket": most underperform, a few
explode. That fits the stage-4 use (read the diff, don't auto-avoid). A mean-based avoid rule would have thrown
away the winners. This was not the pre-registered metric, so it is not a finding.

cos_7 Q1 (−9.5%, t −2.1) comes almost entirely from 2025 filings (−24.7%). It is one of more than 20 secondary
cells, so it is noise until a pre-registered test says otherwise. Do not chase it.

The Bihar Act is a **material external fact absent from the AR** (L40 flag): Bihar is ~17% of GLP and its passage moved the stock (−5 to −11% for
listed MFI lenders on 26/27-Feb-2026, press). It is **not** a licence/lease threat to the core asset (scheduled banks are exempt from its lending
rules), so the card's v1.4 `core_asset_threat` was not set (override log).
